problems.title: Contains Duplicate
problems.problem_statement: Given an integer array nums, return true if any value appears at least twice in the array, and return false if every element is distinct.

core_idea.goal: Determine whether any value repeats in the array.
core_idea.key_insight: A hash set gives O(1) average-case lookup and insertion, so a single pass can catch a repeat the moment it's seen, with no nested loops.
core_idea.trigger_phrase: “Have I seen this value before?” → reach for a Hash Set membership check.

steps: If num is already in h, return True immediately — duplicate found.
If the loop finishes with no match, return False.

walkthrough: Brute force compares every pair of elements, which costs O(n²) time. The moment we're willing to spend O(n) extra space, we can collapse that to a single O(n) pass.

A Python set is backed by a hash table, so num in h and h.add(num) are both O(1) on average. We only need to know “have I seen this number before” — we never need to know where or how many times, so a set is a better fit than a dict or list.
Walk the array once. For each number, check membership before inserting: if it's already there, you've found your duplicate and can short-circuit immediately rather than finishing the scan.
If the loop completes with no early return, every element was unique, so the answer is False.
problems.mental_shortcut: “Seen it before? Set it and forget it.”
problems.interview_talking_point: I'm trading O(n) space for O(n) time with a hash set, which avoids the O(n²) brute-force approach of comparing every pair.
edge_cases: Empty array → no duplicates possible, return False
All elements identical → returns True as soon as the second element is checked
Negative numbers and zero → ints are hashable as-is, no special handling needed

frames.note: Start with an empty hash set h.
num = 1 — not in h, so add it. h = {1}
num = 2 — not in h, so add it. h = {1, 2}
num = 3 — not in h, so add it. h = {1, 2, 3}
num = 1 — already in h! Return True immediately.
